sanskrit: tan nu vo̍cāma rabha̱sāya̱ janma̍ne̱ pūrva̍m mahi̱tvaṁ vṛ̍ṣa̱bhasya̍ ke̱tave̍ | ai̱dheva̱ yāma̍n marutas tuviṣvaṇo yu̱dheva̍ śakrās tavi̱ṣāṇi̍ kartana ||
english: Let us now declare for your impetuous birth the former greatness of the bull, for his banner to be known — even as flames in your course, O Maruts of mighty roar, so, O mighty ones, do you perform powerful deeds as if in battle.

sanskrit: nitya̱ṁ na sū̱num madhu̱ bibhra̍ta̱ upa̱ krīḻa̍nti krī̱ḻā vi̱dathe̍ṣu̱ ghṛṣva̍yaḥ | nakṣa̍nti ru̱drā ava̍sā nama̱svina̱ṁ na ma̍rdhanti̱ svata̍vaso havi̱ṣkṛta̍m ||
english: As if carrying the perpetual honey for a son, they play their games, these spirited ones, in the assemblies. The Rudras reach with their help the devout worshipper; the self-mighty ones do not neglect the sacrificial oblation prepared for them.

sanskrit: yasmā̱ ūmā̍so a̱mṛtā̱ arā̍sata rā̱yas poṣa̍ṁ ca ha̱viṣā̍ dadā̱śuṣe̍ | u̱kṣanty a̍smai ma̱ruto̍ hi̱tā i̍va pu̱rū rajā̍ṁsi̱ paya̍sā mayo̱bhuva̍ḥ ||
english: To him for whom the immortal helpers have granted wealth-abundance, to him who has worshipped with oblation — the Maruts sprinkle for him, as if appointed, the many realms with milk that gives delight.

sanskrit: ā ye rajā̍ṁsi̱ tavi̍ṣībhi̱r avya̍ta̱ pra va̱ evā̍sa̱ḥ svaya̍tāso adhrajan | bhaya̍nte̱ viśvā̱ bhuva̍nāni ha̱rmyā ci̱tro vo̱ yāma̱ḥ praya̍tāsv ṛ̱ṣṭiṣu̍ ||
english: They who filled the realms with their mighty powers — your swift steeds, self-harnessed, rushed forward. All the earthly beings tremble in fear; your march is radiant when your spears are hurled.

sanskrit: yat tve̱ṣayā̍mā na̱daya̍nta̱ parva̍tān di̱vo vā̍ pṛ̱ṣṭhaṁ naryā̱ acu̍cyavuḥ | viśvo̍ vo̱ ajma̍n bhayate̱ vana̱spatī̍ rathī̱yantī̍va̱ pra ji̍hīta̱ oṣa̍dhiḥ ||
english: When in your impetuous course you make the mountains resound and the manly ones have shaken the back of heaven — every forest tree trembles at your onslaught, and the herbs dart forth as if galloping in a chariot-race.

sanskrit: yū̱yaṁ na̍ ugrā marutaḥ suce̱tunāri̍ṣṭagrāmāḥ suma̱tim pi̍partana | yatrā̍ vo di̱dyud rada̍ti̱ krivi̍rdatī ri̱ṇāti̍ pa̱śvaḥ sudhi̍teva ba̱rhaṇā̍ ||
english: Do you, O fierce Maruts, of clear discernment, whose village is unharmed, grant us your favour. Where your lightning gnaws with its sharp teeth, it bursts open the pen of cattle as if with a well-aimed axe.

sanskrit: pra ska̱mbhade̍ṣṇā anava̱bhrarā̍dhaso 'lātṛ̱ṇāso̍ vi̱dathe̍ṣu̱ suṣṭu̍tāḥ | arca̍nty a̱rkam ma̍di̱rasya̍ pī̱taye̍ vi̱dur vī̱rasya̍ pratha̱māni̱ pauṁsyā̍ ||
english: The lavish givers, of unfailing generosity, never diminishing, rightly praised in assemblies — they sing the hymn to drink the exhilarating draught; they have known the foremost manly deeds of the hero.

sanskrit: śa̱tabhu̍jibhi̱s tam a̱bhihru̍ter a̱ghāt pū̱rbhī ra̍kṣatā maruto̱ yam āva̍ta | jana̱ṁ yam u̍grās tavaso virapśinaḥ pā̱thanā̱ śaṁsā̱t tana̍yasya pu̱ṣṭiṣu̍ ||
english: O Maruts, protect with your hundredfold arms from violence and misdeed the one whom you have favoured; the one whom the fierce, mighty, and mighty-bodied ones guard in assemblies from false speech, in the nourishment of his offspring.

sanskrit: viśvā̍ni bha̱drā ma̍ruto̱ rathe̍ṣu vo mitha̱spṛdhye̍va tavi̱ṣāṇy āhi̍tā | aṁse̱ṣv ā va̱ḥ prapa̍theṣu khā̱dayo 'kṣo̍ vaś ca̱krā sa̱mayā̱ vi vā̍vṛte ||
english: All auspicious and mighty things are laid upon your chariots, O Maruts, as if in mutual rivalry. On your shoulders are the bracelets along the ridges, and at once your axle and wheels have turned together.

sanskrit: bhūrī̍ṇi bha̱drā narye̍ṣu bā̱huṣu̱ vakṣa̍ḥsu ru̱kmā ra̍bha̱sāso̍ a̱ñjaya̍ḥ | aṁse̱ṣv etā̍ḥ pa̱viṣu̍ kṣu̱rā adhi̱ vayo̱ na pa̱kṣān vy anu̱ śriyo̍ dhire ||
english: Many auspicious ornaments on their manly arms, golden breastplates on their chests, the impetuous ones anointed — on their shoulders these decorations, razor-blades on their wheels; they have spread their glories like birds spreading their wings.

sanskrit: ma̱hānto̍ ma̱hnā vi̱bhvo̱3̱̍ vibhū̍tayo dūre̱dṛśo̱ ye di̱vyā i̍va̱ stṛbhi̍ḥ | ma̱ndrāḥ su̍ji̱hvāḥ svari̍tāra ā̱sabhi̱ḥ sammi̍ślā̱ indre̍ ma̱ruta̍ḥ pari̱ṣṭubha̍ḥ ||
english: Great in greatness, all-pervading, of all-pervading splendours, seen afar as the heavenly stars — pleasant-voiced, with good tongues, resounding with their lips, the Maruts mingle together with Indra in their surrounding praise.

sanskrit: tad va̍ḥ sujātā maruto mahitva̱naṁ dī̱rghaṁ vo̍ dā̱tram adi̍ter iva vra̱tam | indra̍ś ca̱na tyaja̍sā̱ vi hru̍ṇāti̱ taj janā̍ya̱ yasmai̍ su̱kṛte̱ arā̍dhvam ||
english: That greatness of yours, O well-born Maruts, your generous gift is long as the vow of Aditi; even Indra does not deflect that with violence for the man to whom, for his righteous deed, you have made it available.

sanskrit: tad vo̍ jāmi̱tvam ma̍ruta̱ḥ pare̍ yu̱ge pu̱rū yac chaṁsa̍m amṛtāsa̱ āva̍ta | a̱yā dhi̱yā mana̍ve śru̱ṣṭim āvyā̍ sā̱kaṁ naro̍ da̱ṁsanai̱r ā ci̍kitrire ||
english: That brotherhood of yours, O Maruts, in former ages — you immortals aided many a praiser. With this very prayer, wrapping obedience for Manu, the heroes have shone forth together with wondrous deeds.

sanskrit: yena̍ dī̱rgham ma̍rutaḥ śū̱śavā̍ma yu̱ṣmāke̍na̱ parī̍ṇasā turāsaḥ | ā yat ta̱tana̍n vṛ̱jane̱ janā̍sa e̱bhir ya̱jñebhi̱s tad a̱bhīṣṭi̍m aśyām ||
english: By which, O Maruts, we have long grown strong, the swiftly advancing ones, through your abundance — when the people have spread out in the settlement by these sacrifices — may I attain that desired goal.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa va̱ḥ stomo̍ maruta i̱yaṁ gīr mā̍ndā̱ryasya̍ mā̱nyasya̍ kā̱roḥ | eṣā yā̍sīṣṭa ta̱nve̍ va̱yāṁ vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: This is your praise-song, O Maruts, this is the hymn of Māndārya, the worthy poet. May it go forth for his body as vigour — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: sa̱hasra̍ṁ ta indro̱tayo̍ naḥ sa̱hasra̱ṁ iṣo̍ harivo gū̱rtata̍māḥ | sa̱hasra̱ṁ rāyo̍ māda̱yadhyai̍ saha̱sriṇa̱ upa̍ no yantu̱ vājā̍ḥ ||
english: A thousand of your helps be ours, O Indra; a thousand refreshments, O bay-horsed one, most welcome of all! A thousand of riches to rejoice in — may thousandfold prizes come to us.

sanskrit: ā no 'vo̍bhir ma̱ruto̍ yā̱ntv acchā̱ jyeṣṭhe̍bhir vā bṛ̱haddi̍vaiḥ sumā̱yāḥ | adha̱ yad e̍ṣāṁ ni̱yuta̍ḥ para̱māḥ sa̍mu̱drasya̍ cid dha̱naya̍nta pā̱re ||
english: May the Maruts come towards us with their aids, or with their great-shining eldest ones, wise in their ways — even when their most distant teams rush thundering on the far shore of the ocean.

sanskrit: mi̱myakṣa̱ yeṣu̱ sudhi̍tā ghṛ̱tācī̱ hira̍ṇyanirṇi̱g upa̍rā̱ na ṛ̱ṣṭiḥ | guhā̱ cara̍ntī̱ manu̍ṣo̱ na yoṣā̍ sa̱bhāva̍tī vida̱thye̍va̱ saṁ vāk ||
english: Among them has come the well-placed ghee-streaming one, golden-robed, like an uplifted spear — moving in secret like a woman of Manu, the speech comes together in the assembly like one meant for an assembly.

sanskrit: parā̍ śu̱bhrā a̱yāso̍ ya̱vyā sā̍dhāra̱ṇyeva̍ ma̱ruto̍ mimikṣuḥ | na ro̍da̱sī apa̍ nudanta gho̱rā ju̱ṣanta̱ vṛdha̍ṁ sa̱khyāya̍ de̱vāḥ ||
english: The bright, impetuous ones have poured out far and wide as if sharing a common path, O Maruts. The terrible ones did not drive away the two worlds; the gods joyfully embraced their growth in friendship.

sanskrit: joṣa̱d yad ī̍m asu̱ryā̍ sa̱cadhyai̱ viṣi̍tastukā roda̱sī nṛ̱maṇā̍ḥ | ā sū̱ryeva̍ vidha̱to ratha̍ṁ gāt tve̱ṣapra̍tīkā̱ nabha̍so̱ netyā ||
english: When the mighty lady of sovereignty desired to join them, with hair dishevelled, the two worlds taking delight in heroes — she came like the sun going to the worshipper's chariot, with a blazing countenance, not to be led back from the sky.

sanskrit: āsthā̍payanta yuva̱tiṁ yuvā̍naḥ śu̱bhe nimi̍ślāṁ vi̱dathe̍ṣu pa̱jrām | a̱rko yad vo̍ maruto ha̱viṣmā̱n gāya̍d gā̱thaṁ su̱taso̍mo duva̱syan ||
english: The young ones have caused the maiden to stand, the Pajra woman veiled for beauty in the assemblies — when the oblation-bearer, the singer of the Pajra clan, sings a song for you, O Maruts, with pressed soma, honouring you.

sanskrit: pra taṁ vi̍vakmi̱ vakmyo̱ ya e̍ṣām ma̱rutā̍m mahi̱mā sa̱tyo asti̍ | sacā̱ yad ī̱ṁ vṛṣa̍maṇā aha̱ṁyuḥ sthi̱rā ci̱j janī̱r vaha̍te subhā̱gāḥ ||
english: I declare him worthy of speech whose true glory of these Maruts exists — when he, the bull-spirited one, self-glorious, bears along even steady women, the fortunate ones, in his company.

sanskrit: pānti̍ mi̱trāvaru̍ṇāv ava̱dyāc caya̍ta īm arya̱mo apra̍śastān | u̱ta cya̍vante̱ acyu̍tā dhru̱vāṇi̍ vāvṛ̱dha ī̍m maruto̱ dāti̍vāraḥ ||
english: Mitra and Varuṇa protect from reproach; Aryaman keeps down the unworthy. And even the immovable, fixed things are shaken; the Maruts, lavish givers, have grown mightily.

sanskrit: na̱hī nu vo̍ maruto̱ anty a̱sme ā̱rāttā̍c ci̱c chava̍so̱ anta̍m ā̱puḥ | te dhṛ̱ṣṇunā̱ śava̍sā śūśu̱vāṁso 'rṇo̱ na dveṣo̍ dhṛṣa̱tā pari̍ ṣṭhuḥ ||
english: Indeed, O Maruts, none among us, even from afar, has reached the end of your might. They who have grown great with bold strength stand around hatred as around a flood, boldly.

sanskrit: va̱yam a̱dyendra̍sya̱ preṣṭhā̍ va̱yaṁ śvo vo̍cemahi sama̱rye | va̱yaṁ pu̱rā mahi̍ ca no̱ anu̱ dyūn tan na̍ ṛbhu̱kṣā na̱rām anu̍ ṣyāt ||
english: Today we would proclaim ourselves the dearest of Indra; tomorrow in the assembly we would say the same. May that greatness of ours be with us through all the days; may the Ṛbhukṣan, lord of men, follow us therein.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa va̱ḥ stomo̍ maruta i̱yaṁ gīr mā̍ndā̱ryasya̍ mā̱nyasya̍ kā̱roḥ | eṣā yā̍sīṣṭa ta̱nve̍ va̱yāṁ vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: This is your praise-song, O Maruts, this is the hymn of Māndārya, the worthy poet. May it go forth for his body as vigour — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: ya̱jñā-ya̍jñā vaḥ sama̱nā tu̍tu̱rvaṇi̱r dhiya̍ṁ-dhiyaṁ vo deva̱yā u̍ dadhidhve | ā vo̱ 'rvāca̍ḥ suvi̱tāya̱ roda̍syor ma̱he va̍vṛtyā̱m ava̍se suvṛ̱ktibhi̍ḥ ||
english: At each and every sacrifice, hastening to your common gathering, the god-seeking one lays down thought after thought for you. I would turn you hither-ward for our welfare, with beautiful verses, for the help of the two worlds, for great protection.

sanskrit: va̱vrāso̱ na ye sva̱jāḥ svata̍vasa̱ iṣa̱ṁ sva̍r abhi̱jāya̍nta̱ dhūta̍yaḥ | sa̱ha̱sriyā̍so a̱pāṁ normaya̍ ā̱sā gāvo̱ vandyā̍so̱ nokṣaṇa̍ḥ ||
english: Like covered ones of their own kind, the self-mighty, shakers, have won refreshment and the sun. Thousandfold like waves of the waters with their mouths — cows worthy of reverence, and bulls.

sanskrit: somā̍so̱ na ye su̱tās tṛ̱ptāṁśa̍vo hṛ̱tsu pī̱tāso̍ du̱vaso̱ nāsa̍te | aiṣā̱m aṁse̍ṣu ra̱mbhiṇī̍va rārabhe̱ haste̍ṣu khā̱diś ca̍ kṛ̱tiś ca̱ saṁ da̍dhe ||
english: Like pressed soma juices, they whose limbs are satisfied, who have drunk to the heart, who serve — they do not sit idle. On their shoulders, as if clasping, is fixed the decoration; in their hands, the bracelet and the sword are joined together.

sanskrit: ava̱ svayu̍ktā di̱va ā vṛthā̍ yayu̱r ama̍rtyā̱ḥ kaśa̍yā codata̱ tmanā̍ | a̱re̱ṇava̍s tuvijā̱tā a̍cucyavur dṛ̱ḻhāni̍ cin ma̱ruto̱ bhrāja̍dṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: The immortals, self-harnessed, have gone down freely from heaven, urged onward by a whip of their own accord. Dustless, born in might, the Maruts of flashing spears have shaken even what is firm and fixed.

sanskrit: ko vo̱ 'ntar ma̍ruta ṛṣṭividyuto̱ reja̍ti̱ tmanā̱ hanve̍va ji̱hvayā̍ | dha̱nva̱cyuta̍ i̱ṣāṁ na yāma̍ni puru̱praiṣā̍ aha̱nyo̱3̱̍ naita̍śaḥ ||
english: Who trembles of himself among you, O Maruts of lightning spears, as if with a tongue in the jaw? Swept from the desert in the rush of the courses, the never-sleeping Naitaśa calls on many to advance.

sanskrit: kva̍ svid a̱sya raja̍so ma̱has para̱ṁ kvāva̍ram maruto̱ yasmi̍nn āya̱ya | yac cyā̱vaya̍tha vithu̱reva̱ saṁhi̍ta̱ṁ vy adri̍ṇā patatha tve̱ṣam a̍rṇa̱vam ||
english: Where is the farther limit of this great realm, and where the nearer, O Maruts, in which you go about? When you set tottering what seemed fixed together and fly apart, cleaving the terrible ocean with your stone.

sanskrit: sā̱tir na vo 'ma̍vatī̱ sva̍rvatī tve̱ṣā vipā̍kā maruta̱ḥ pipi̍ṣvatī | bha̱drā vo̍ rā̱tiḥ pṛ̍ṇa̱to na dakṣi̍ṇā pṛthu̱jrayī̍ asu̱rye̍va̱ jañja̍tī ||
english: Your winning is filled with violence and solar light, O Maruts, blazing and all-ripening, swelling. Your bounty to the worshipper is auspicious as a sacrificial gift, spreading wide its way, crackling as if with sovereign power.

sanskrit: prati̍ ṣṭobhanti̱ sindha̍vaḥ pa̱vibhyo̱ yad a̱bhriyā̱ṁ vāca̍m udī̱raya̍nti | ava̍ smayanta vi̱dyuta̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyāṁ yadī̍ ghṛ̱tam ma̱ruta̍ḥ pruṣṇu̱vanti̍ ||
english: The rivers resound back from their wheel-rims when you raise the cloud-born voice. The lightnings smile downward upon the earth whenever the Maruts sprinkle their ghee.

sanskrit: asū̍ta̱ pṛśni̍r maha̱te raṇā̍ya tve̱ṣam a̱yāsā̍m ma̱rutā̱m anī̍kam | te sa̍psa̱rāso̍ 'janaya̱ntābhva̱m ād it sva̱dhām i̍ṣi̱rām pary a̍paśyan ||
english: Pṛśni bore for the great battle the blazing host of the impetuous Maruts. They, of fair appearance, brought forth the monstrous thing; and then they looked around upon their vigorous power.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa va̱ḥ stomo̍ maruta i̱yaṁ gīr mā̍ndā̱ryasya̍ mā̱nyasya̍ kā̱roḥ | eṣā yā̍sīṣṭa ta̱nve̍ va̱yāṁ vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: This is your praise-song, O Maruts, this is the hymn of Māndārya, the worthy poet. May it go forth for his body as vigour — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: ma̱haś ci̱t tvam i̍ndra ya̱ta e̱tān ma̱haś ci̍d asi̱ tyaja̍so varū̱tā | sa no̍ vedho ma̱rutā̍ṁ ciki̱tvān su̱mnā va̍nuṣva̱ tava̱ hi preṣṭhā̍ ||
english: Great as you are, O Indra, when you go to these great ones — great too are you as the protector from their abandonment. Knowing the Maruts, O wise one, win for us your blessings; they are indeed your most beloved.

sanskrit: ayu̍jran ta indra vi̱śvakṛ̍ṣṭīr vidā̱nāso̍ ni̱ṣṣidho̍ martya̱trā | ma̱rutā̍m pṛtsu̱tir hāsa̍mānā̱ sva̍rmīḻhasya pra̱dhana̍sya sā̱tau ||
english: They have yoked your teams, O Indra, among all peoples, knowing the hindrance among mortals. The battle-cry of the Maruts is laughing out in the contest for the winning of the heavenly, bountiful prize of battle.

sanskrit: amya̱k sā ta̍ indra ṛ̱ṣṭir a̱sme sane̱my abhva̍m ma̱ruto̍ junanti | a̱gniś ci̱d dhi ṣmā̍ta̱se śu̍śu̱kvān āpo̱ na dvī̱paṁ dadha̍ti̱ prayā̍ṁsi ||
english: Straight toward us is that spear of yours, O Indra; the Maruts urge the monstrous one onward unwaveringly. For Agni, indeed, blazing for him, lay their offerings like waters around an island.

sanskrit: tvaṁ tū na̍ indra̱ taṁ ra̱yiṁ dā̱ oji̍ṣṭhayā̱ dakṣi̍ṇayeva rā̱tim | stuta̍ś ca̱ yās te̍ ca̱kana̍nta vā̱yoḥ stana̱ṁ na madhva̍ḥ pīpayanta̱ vājai̍ḥ ||
english: But do you, O Indra, give us that wealth as a gift with your most powerful right hand. And those that have taken delight in being praised by you have nourished prizes like the honey-sweet breast of Vāyu.

sanskrit: tve rāya̍ indra to̱śata̍māḥ praṇe̱tāra̱ḥ kasya̍ cid ṛtā̱yoḥ | te ṣu ṇo̍ ma̱ruto̍ mṛḻayantu̱ ye smā̍ pu̱rā gā̍tū̱yantī̍va de̱vāḥ ||
english: In you, O Indra, the most enriching leaders of any righteous man reside. May those Maruts be gracious to us — those gods who of old moved as if seeking a path.

sanskrit: prati̱ pra yā̍hīndra mī̱ḻhuṣo̱ nṝn ma̱haḥ pārthi̍ve̱ sada̍ne yatasva | adha̱ yad e̍ṣāṁ pṛthubu̱dhnāsa̱ etā̍s tī̱rthe nāryaḥ pauṁsyā̍ni ta̱sthuḥ ||
english: Go forward to meet the bountiful heroes, O Indra; strive in the great earthly seat. And where these broad-based streams have stood at the ford with their manly deeds —

sanskrit: prati̍ gho̱rāṇā̱m etā̍nām a̱yāsā̍m ma̱rutā̍ṁ śṛṇva āya̱tām u̍pa̱bdiḥ | ye martya̍m pṛtanā̱yanta̱m ūmai̍r ṛṇā̱vāna̱ṁ na pa̱taya̍nta̱ sargai̍ḥ ||
english: I hear the approaching thunder of these terrible, impetuous Maruts coming. They who with their helps fling down the mortal who fights against them like a debtor with their rushing charges.

sanskrit: tvam māne̍bhya indra vi̱śvaja̍nyā̱ radā̍ ma̱rudbhi̍ḥ śu̱rudho̱ goa̍grāḥ | stavā̍nebhiḥ stavase deva de̱vair vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: Grant us, O Indra, together with the Maruts, all-people riches, the roaring gifts that have cattle at their head. O god, you are praised by those who praise you, by the gods — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: na nū̱nam asti̱ no śvaḥ kas tad ve̍da̱ yad adbhu̍tam | a̱nyasya̍ ci̱ttam a̱bhi sa̍ṁca̱reṇya̍m u̱tādhī̍ta̱ṁ vi na̍śyati ||
english: There is neither now nor tomorrow — who knows what is wonderful? The mind of another is not to be approached, and even what is well pondered vanishes.

sanskrit: kiṁ na̍ indra jighāṁsasi̱ bhrāta̍ro ma̱ruta̱s tava̍ | tebhi̍ḥ kalpasva sādhu̱yā mā na̍ḥ sa̱mara̍ṇe vadhīḥ ||
english: Why, O Indra, do you wish to strike us? The Maruts are your brothers. With them act rightly — do not slay us at the encounter.

sanskrit: kiṁ no̍ bhrātar agastya̱ sakhā̱ sann ati̍ manyase | vi̱dmā hi te̱ yathā̱ mano̱ 'smabhya̱m in na di̍tsasi ||
english: Why, O brother Agastya, being our friend, do you think too highly of yourself? We know your mind — you do not wish to give to us.

sanskrit: ara̍ṁ kṛṇvantu̱ vedi̱ṁ sam a̱gnim i̍ndhatām pu̱raḥ | tatrā̱mṛta̍sya̱ ceta̍naṁ ya̱jñaṁ te̍ tanavāvahai ||
english: Let them prepare the altar; let them kindle Agni in front. There, with awareness of the immortal, let us two spread out the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tvam ī̍śiṣe vasupate̱ vasū̍nā̱ṁ tvam mi̱trāṇā̍m mitrapate̱ dheṣṭha̍ḥ | indra̱ tvam ma̱rudbhi̱ḥ saṁ va̍da̱svādha̱ prāśā̍na ṛtu̱thā ha̱vīṁṣi̍ ||
english: You are the lord of riches, O lord of wealth; you are the best bestower of friendship, O lord of friends. O Indra, agree together with the Maruts; thereafter eat the oblations each in due season.

sanskrit: prati̍ va e̱nā nama̍sā̱ham e̍mi sū̱ktena̍ bhikṣe suma̱tiṁ tu̱rāṇā̍m | ra̱rā̱ṇatā̍ maruto ve̱dyābhi̱r ni heḻo̍ dha̱tta vi mu̍cadhva̱m aśvā̍n ||
english: I come to you with reverence and with a well-spoken hymn I implore the favour of the swift ones. O Maruts, who rejoice in what is to be known, lay aside your anger and unyoke your horses.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa va̱ḥ stomo̍ maruto̱ nama̍svān hṛ̱dā ta̱ṣṭo mana̍sā dhāyi devāḥ | upe̱m ā yā̍ta̱ mana̍sā juṣā̱ṇā yū̱yaṁ hi ṣṭhā nama̍sa̱ id vṛ̱dhāsa̍ḥ ||
english: This your reverent praise-song, O Maruts, fashioned from the heart, has been set by the mind, O gods. Come hither pleased in mind; for you are indeed those who grow great through worship.

sanskrit: stu̱tāso̍ no ma̱ruto̍ mṛḻayantū̱ta stu̱to ma̱ghavā̱ śambha̍viṣṭhaḥ | ū̱rdhvā na̍ḥ santu ko̱myā vanā̱ny ahā̍ni̱ viśvā̍ maruto jigī̱ṣā ||
english: May the Maruts, praised, be gracious to us; and may the praised Maghavan be most gracious. May our desirable forests rise upward; may we be victorious, O Maruts, through all the days.

sanskrit: a̱smād a̱haṁ ta̍vi̱ṣād īṣa̍māṇa̱ indrā̍d bhi̱yā ma̍ruto̱ reja̍mānaḥ | yu̱ṣmabhya̍ṁ ha̱vyā niśi̍tāny āsa̱n tāny ā̱re ca̍kṛmā mṛ̱ḻatā̍ naḥ ||
english: Fleeing from this mighty power, trembling in fear of Indra, O Maruts — the oblations that were prepared for you, those I have set far away. Be gracious to us.

sanskrit: yena̱ mānā̍saś ci̱taya̍nta u̱srā vyu̍ṣṭiṣu̱ śava̍sā̱ śaśva̍tīnām | sa no̍ ma̱rudbhi̍r vṛṣabha̱ śravo̍ dhā u̱gra u̱grebhi̱ḥ sthavi̍raḥ saho̱dāḥ ||
english: By whom the cows are made to shine at the dawnings of the perpetual ones with power — do you, O bull, mighty, firm and strong-giving, establish fame for us with the Maruts, together with the fierce ones.

sanskrit: tvam pā̍hīndra̱ sahī̍yaso̱ nṝn bhavā̍ ma̱rudbhi̱r ava̍yātaheḻāḥ | su̱pra̱ke̱tebhi̍ḥ sāsa̱hir dadhā̍no vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: Protect us, O Indra, protect the mighty men; together with the Maruts let your anger be appeased. Conquering, holding with clear wisdom — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: ci̱tro vo̍ 'stu̱ yāma̍ś ci̱tra ū̱tī su̍dānavaḥ | maru̍to̱ ahi̍bhānavaḥ ||
english: Radiant be your march and radiant your help, O generous givers! O Maruts shining like serpents!

sanskrit: ā̱re sā va̍ḥ sudānavo̱ maru̍ta ṛñja̱tī śaru̍ḥ | ā̱re aśmā̱ yam asya̍tha ||
english: Far from you, O generous Maruts, is the gleaming arrow; far is the stone that you hurl.

sanskrit: tṛ̱ṇa̱ska̱ndasya̱ nu viśa̱ḥ pari̍ vṛṅkta sudānavaḥ | ū̱rdhvān na̍ḥ karta jī̱vase̍ ||
english: Turn away the people of Tṛṇaskanda now, O generous givers; raise us up to live.

sanskrit: gāya̱t sāma̍ nabha̱nya1̱̍ṁ yathā̱ ver arcā̍ma̱ tad vā̍vṛdhā̱naṁ sva̍rvat | gāvo̍ dhe̱navo̍ ba̱rhiṣy ada̍bdhā̱ ā yat sa̱dmāna̍ṁ di̱vyaṁ vivā̍sān ||
english: As a bird sings a heavenly sāman, let us praise that which has grown great, possessed of the sun — when the undeceived milch-cows come to the kusa grass, worshipping the heavenly seat.

sanskrit: arca̱d vṛṣā̱ vṛṣa̍bhi̱ḥ svedu̍havyair mṛ̱go nāśno̱ ati̱ yaj ju̍gu̱ryāt | pra ma̍nda̱yur ma̱nāṁ gū̍rta̱ hotā̱ bhara̍te̱ maryo̍ mithu̱nā yaja̍traḥ ||
english: The bull has sung with bulls and with sweet-smelling oblations — as a wild beast goes past those that eat, surpassing. The gladdening, welcome Hotā bears the mind; the worshipful young man bears the pair.

sanskrit: nakṣa̱d dhotā̱ pari̱ sadma̍ mi̱tā yan bhara̱d garbha̱m ā śa̱rada̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyāḥ | kranda̱d aśvo̱ naya̍māno ru̱vad gaur a̱ntar dū̱to na roda̍sī cara̱d vāk ||
english: The Hotā reaches around the measured seat as he goes, bearing the embryo of the autumns of the earth. The horse neighs and the cow lows as it is led; the speech moves as a messenger between the two worlds.

sanskrit: tā ka̱rmāṣa̍tarāsmai̱ pra cyau̱tnāni̍ deva̱yanto̍ bharante | jujo̍ṣa̱d indro̍ da̱smava̍rcā̱ nāsa̍tyeva̱ sugmyo̍ rathe̱ṣṭhāḥ ||
english: Those of variegated acts bear forward impulses for him who is devoted to the gods. Indra of wondrous brilliance has rejoiced, easy to invoke like the Nāsatyas, standing on the chariot.

sanskrit: tam u̍ ṣṭu̱hīndra̱ṁ yo ha̱ satvā̱ yaḥ śūro̍ ma̱ghavā̱ yo ra̍the̱ṣṭhāḥ | pra̱tī̱caś ci̱d yodhī̍yā̱n vṛṣa̍ṇvān vava̱vruṣa̍ś ci̱t tama̍so viha̱ntā ||
english: Praise that Indra who is a real fighter, who is a hero, who is the bountiful one, who stands on his chariot. Most martial even against those who face him, the bull-endowed destroyer even of those hidden in darkness.

sanskrit: pra yad i̱tthā ma̍hi̱nā nṛbhyo̱ asty ara̱ṁ roda̍sī ka̱kṣye̱3̱̍ nāsmai̍ | saṁ vi̍vya̱ indro̍ vṛ̱jana̱ṁ na bhūmā̱ bharti̍ sva̱dhāvā̍m̐ opa̱śam i̍va̱ dyām ||
english: When thus he is great enough for the heroes, the two worlds are not sufficient for his girth. Indra wrapped around the settlement as the earth does; the self-powerful one supports the branch of the sky.

sanskrit: sa̱matsu̍ tvā śūra sa̱tām u̍rā̱ṇam pra̍pa̱thinta̍mam paritaṁsa̱yadhyai̍ | sa̱joṣa̍sa̱ indra̱m made̍ kṣo̱ṇīḥ sū̱riṁ ci̱d ye a̍nu̱mada̍nti̱ vājai̍ḥ ||
english: In battles, O hero, let the most liberal among those who are generous be wrapped around you to embrace you. Those who rejoice over Indra together in exhilaration in the domains — and who exult even over the sun-lord with prizes.

sanskrit: e̱vā hi te̱ śaṁ sava̍nā samu̱dra āpo̱ yat ta̍ ā̱su mada̍nti de̱vīḥ | viśvā̍ te̱ anu̱ joṣyā̍ bhū̱d gauḥ sū̱rīm̐ś ci̱d yadi̍ dhi̱ṣā veṣi̱ janā̍n ||
english: For thus are your pressings blissful as an ocean in which the divine waters rejoice for you. The cow has been for you in all respects a source of delight — even when with wisdom you seek out the sun-lords among the people.

sanskrit: asā̍ma̱ yathā̍ suṣa̱khāya̍ ena svabhi̱ṣṭayo̍ na̱rāṁ na śaṁsai̍ḥ | asa̱d yathā̍ na̱ indro̍ vandane̱ṣṭhās tu̱ro na karma̱ naya̍māna u̱kthā ||
english: May we be for you as good friends, with our own power of men not to be overcome by praises — may Indra be for us one who stands in praise, swift as one who leads in the work, with songs of praise.

sanskrit: viṣpa̍rdhaso na̱rāṁ na śaṁsai̍r a̱smākā̍sa̱d indro̱ vajra̍hastaḥ | mi̱trā̱yuvo̱ na pūrpa̍ti̱ṁ suśi̍ṣṭau madhyā̱yuva̱ upa̍ śikṣanti ya̱jñaiḥ ||
english: The rival among men, not to be overcome by praises — may Indra of the thunderbolt hand be ours. Like those who seek a friend, those who seek the lord of the city, those who have learned the proper way, worship the middle-seeking ones with sacrifices.

sanskrit: ya̱jño hi ṣmendra̱ṁ kaś ci̍d ṛ̱ndhañ ju̍hurā̱ṇaś ci̱n mana̍sā pari̱yan ||  tī̱rthe nācchā̍ tātṛṣā̱ṇam oko̍ dī̱rgho na si̱dhram ā kṛ̍ṇo̱ty adhvā̍ ||
english: Indeed, whatever sacrifice enriches Indra, even the one who pours, going around with his mind — as one thirsting does not find his home at the ford, so the long path makes him helpless.

sanskrit: mo ṣū ṇa̍ i̱ndrātra̍ pṛ̱tsu de̱vair asti̱ hi ṣmā̍ te śuṣminn ava̱yāḥ | ma̱haś ci̱d yasya̍ mī̱ḻhuṣo̍ ya̱vyā ha̱viṣma̍to ma̱ruto̱ vanda̍te̱ gīḥ ||
english: Do not abandon us here, O Indra, in battles with the gods; for there is indeed that which wards off your strength. Even the great bountiful one — for whose eager one the Maruts' praise from the oblation-bearer finds its mark.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa stoma̍ indra̱ tubhya̍m a̱sme e̱tena̍ gā̱tuṁ ha̍rivo vido naḥ | ā no̍ vavṛtyāḥ suvi̱tāya̍ deva vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: This praise-song, O Indra, is for you from us; by means of it, O bay-horsed one, find a path for us. Turn toward us for our welfare, O god — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: tvaṁ rāje̍ndra̱ ye ca̍ de̱vā rakṣā̱ nṝn pā̱hy a̍sura̱ tvam a̱smān | tvaṁ satpa̍tir ma̱ghavā̍ na̱s taru̍tra̱s tvaṁ sa̱tyo vasa̍vānaḥ saho̱dāḥ ||
english: You, O Indra, are the king, and the gods protect — protect the men, O Asura, protect us. You are the true lord, O bountiful protector of ours; you are the true one, bringing wealth, the strength-giver.

sanskrit: dano̱ viśa̍ indra mṛ̱dhravā̍caḥ sa̱pta yat pura̱ḥ śarma̱ śāra̍dī̱r dart | ṛ̱ṇor a̱po a̍nava̱dyārṇā̱ yūne̍ vṛ̱tram pu̍ru̱kutsā̍ya randhīḥ ||
english: O Indra, you drove away the peoples of hostile speech; you split open the seven autumnal forts for shelter. You released the blameless, wave-like waters for the young man; you subdued Vṛtra for Purukutsa.

sanskrit: ajā̱ vṛta̍ indra̱ śūra̍patnī̱r dyāṁ ca̱ yebhi̍ḥ puruhūta nū̱nam | rakṣo̍ a̱gnim a̱śuṣa̱ṁ tūrva̍yāṇaṁ si̱ṁho na dame̱ apā̍ṁsi̱ vasto̍ḥ ||
english: Drive away, O Indra, the wives of the heroes, and also heaven with them now, O much-invoked one. The Rakṣas, the fire that does not dry up, the overpowering one — like a lion in the house, drive away those active in the night.

sanskrit: śeṣa̱n nu ta i‍ndra̱ sasmi̱n yonau̱ praśa̍staye̱ pavī̍ravasya ma̱hnā | sṛ̱jad arṇā̱ṁsy ava̱ yad yu̱dhā gās tiṣṭha̱d dharī̍ dhṛṣa̱tā mṛ̍ṣṭa̱ vājā̍n ||
english: The remainders rest now in their common womb for your glory, O Indra, by the greatness of the thunderbolt. When in battle he released the rivers that had cattle, the bay horses stood boldly, winning prizes.

sanskrit: vaha̱ kutsa̍m indra̱ yasmi̍ñ cā̱kan syū̍ma̱nyū ṛ̱jrā vāta̱syāśvā̍ | pra sūra̍ś ca̱kraṁ vṛ̍hatād a̱bhīke̱ 'bhi spṛdho̍ yāsiṣa̱d vajra̍bāhuḥ ||
english: Carry Kutsa, O Indra, in whom you took delight, in the harness of the Syūmanyu, with the bright horses of the wind. Let the sun roll forward the wheel in the encounter; may the thunderbolt-armed one advance against the rivals.

sanskrit: ja̱gha̱nvām̐ i̍ndra mi̱trerū̍ñ co̱dapra̍vṛddho harivo̱ adā̍śūn | pra ye paśya̍nn arya̱maṇa̱ṁ sacā̱yos tvayā̍ śū̱rtā vaha̍mānā̱ apa̍tyam ||
english: Slaying those who have the friendship of enemies, O Indra, bay-horsed, impelled to give, those who do not offer. Those who, seeing Aryaman of the companions, are carried off by you in the rush, bearing offspring.

sanskrit: rapa̍t ka̱vir i̍ndrā̱rkasā̍tau̱ kṣāṁ dā̱sāyo̍pa̱barha̍ṇīṁ kaḥ | kara̍t ti̱sro ma̱ghavā̱ dānu̍citrā̱ ni du̍ryo̱ṇe kuya̍vācam mṛ̱dhi śre̍t ||
english: The wise one stumbled at the battle for the sun; he made the earth a couch for the Dāsa. The bountiful one made the three waters brilliant with gifts; in the dwelling of evil deeds he crushed him who speaks ill.

sanskrit: sanā̱ tā ta̍ indra̱ navyā̱ āgu̱ḥ saho̱ nabho 'vi̍raṇāya pū̱rvīḥ ||  bhi̱nat puro̱ na bhido̱ ade̍vīr na̱namo̱ vadha̱r ade̍vasya pī̱yoḥ ||
english: Old as they are, those powers of yours, O Indra, have come as new; strength and cloud, many, to not perish. He split apart the godless forts, not breakable; the weapon bowed not before the taunting of the ungodly.

sanskrit: tvaṁ dhuni̍r indra̱ dhuni̍matīr ṛ̱ṇor a̱paḥ sī̱rā na srava̍ntīḥ | pra yat sa̍mu̱dram ati̍ śūra̱ parṣi̍ pā̱rayā̍ tu̱rvaśa̱ṁ yadu̍ṁ sva̱sti ||
english: You, O Indra, are the roarer; you have set the roaring waters free, flowing like rivers. When you carry across the ocean, O hero, bring Turvaśa and Yadu over safely.

sanskrit: tvam a̱smāka̍m indra vi̱śvadha̍ syā avṛ̱kata̍mo na̱rāṁ nṛ̍pā̱tā | sa no̱ viśvā̍sāṁ spṛ̱dhāṁ sa̍ho̱dā vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: Be you ours always in all ways, O Indra, the most free from entanglement, the protector of men. Do you, the strength-giver of all conflicts, grant us — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: matsy apā̍yi te̱ maha̱ḥ pātra̍syeva harivo matsa̱ro mada̍ḥ | vṛṣā̍ te̱ vṛṣṇa̱ indu̍r vā̱jī sa̍hasra̱sāta̍maḥ ||
english: The intoxicating exhilaration of your great vessel has been drunk, O bay-horsed one, like that of a great cup. Your drop, O bull among bulls, is the racer that wins the thousandfold prize.

sanskrit: ā na̍s te gantu matsa̱ro vṛṣā̱ mado̱ vare̍ṇyaḥ | sa̱hāvā̍m̐ indra sāna̱siḥ pṛ̍tanā̱ṣāḻ ama̍rtyaḥ ||
english: Let there come to us your exhilarating, bull-like, desirable intoxication — conquering, O Indra, ever-winning, crushing armies, immortal.

sanskrit: tvaṁ hi śūra̱ḥ sani̍tā co̱dayo̱ manu̍ṣo̱ ratha̍m | sa̱hāvā̱n dasyu̍m avra̱tam oṣa̱ḥ pātra̱ṁ na śo̱ciṣā̍ ||
english: For you are the hero, the winner, you who impel the chariot of Manu; conquering, you burn the lawless Dasyu like a vessel with your flame.

sanskrit: mu̱ṣā̱ya sūrya̍ṁ kave ca̱kram īśā̍na̱ oja̍sā | vaha̱ śuṣṇā̍ya va̱dhaṁ kutsa̱ṁ vāta̱syāśvai̍ḥ ||
english: You who are wise, you stole the sun, wielding the wheel with your might; you brought the weapon to Śuṣṇa, carrying Kutsa with the horses of the wind.

sanskrit: śu̱ṣminta̍mo̱ hi te̱ mado̍ dyu̱mninta̍ma u̱ta kratu̍ḥ | vṛ̱tra̱ghnā va̍rivo̱vidā̍ maṁsī̱ṣṭhā a̍śva̱sāta̍maḥ ||
english: For your exhilaration is most vigorous and most glorious, and so is your wisdom — O Vṛtra-slayer, finder of wide space, most glorious, winning most horses.

sanskrit: yathā̱ pūrve̍bhyo jari̱tṛbhya̍ indra̱ maya̍ i̱vāpo̱ na tṛṣya̍te ba̱bhūtha̍ | tām anu̍ tvā ni̱vida̍ṁ johavīmi vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: As you have been for the praisers of old, O Indra, like a delight, like waters for one who does not thirst — following that I call you with the Nivid formula: may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: matsi̍ no̱ vasya̍ïṣṭaya̱ indra̍m indo̱ vṛṣā vi̍śa | ṛ̱ghā̱yamā̍ṇa invasi̱ śatru̱m anti̱ na vi̍ndasi ||
english: Exhilarate Indra for us for the desire of better things, O drop, O bull — enter in! While you roam about raging, you find no enemy near.

sanskrit: tasmi̱nn ā ve̍śayā̱ giro̱ ya eka̍ś carṣaṇī̱nām | anu̍ sva̱dhā yam u̱pyate̱ yava̱ṁ na carkṛ̍ṣa̱d vṛṣā̍ ||
english: Into him bestow your songs — him who is the sole one of the tribes. According to his own power the bull is cultivated, as barley is ploughed over and over.

sanskrit: yasya̱ viśvā̍ni̱ hasta̍yo̱ḥ pañca̍ kṣitī̱nāṁ vasu̍ | spā̱śaya̍sva̱ yo a̍sma̱dhrug di̱vyevā̱śani̍r jahi ||
english: In whose two hands lie all the wealth of the five peoples — search out him who is our enemy; smite him like a heavenly thunderbolt.

sanskrit: asu̍nvantaṁ samaṁ jahi dū̱ṇāśa̱ṁ yo na te̱ maya̍ḥ | a̱smabhya̍m asya̱ veda̍naṁ da̱ddhi sū̱riś ci̍d ohate ||
english: Strike down the non-presser, the equal one, who is distressingly not delightful to you. Give us his treasure; even the sun-lord praises this.

sanskrit: āvo̱ yasya̍ dvi̱barha̍so̱ 'rkeṣu̍ sānu̱ṣag asa̍t | ā̱jāv indra̍syendo̱ prāvo̱ vāje̍ṣu vā̱jina̍m ||
english: You aided him whose doubled might was continuous in the hymns — O drop, in the race you helped the prize-winner of Indra in the prizes.

sanskrit: yathā̱ pūrve̍bhyo jari̱tṛbhya̍ indra̱ maya̍ i̱vāpo̱ na tṛṣya̍te ba̱bhūtha̍ | tām anu̍ tvā ni̱vida̍ṁ johavīmi vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: As you have been for the praisers of old, O Indra, like a delight, like waters for one who does not thirst — following that I call you with the Nivid formula: may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: ā ca̍rṣaṇi̱prā vṛ̍ṣa̱bho janā̍nā̱ṁ rājā̍ kṛṣṭī̱nām pu̍ruhū̱ta indra̍ḥ | stu̱taḥ śra̍va̱syann ava̱sopa̍ ma̱drig yu̱ktvā harī̱ vṛṣa̱ṇā yā̍hy a̱rvāṅ ||
english: Filling the peoples full, the bull of men, the king of the tribes, much-invoked Indra — praised, seeking glory with help — harnessing the two bull-like bay steeds, come hither!

sanskrit: ye te̱ vṛṣa̍ṇo vṛṣa̱bhāsa̍ indra brahma̱yujo̱ vṛṣa̍rathāso̱ atyā̍ḥ | tām̐ ā ti̍ṣṭha̱ tebhi̱r ā yā̍hy a̱rvāṅ havā̍mahe tvā su̱ta i̍ndra̱ some̍ ||
english: Your bulls, O Indra, those bull-like stallions harnessed by prayer, drawing the bull's chariot — mount them and come hither! We invoke you at the pressed soma, O Indra.

sanskrit: ā ti̍ṣṭha̱ ratha̱ṁ vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ vṛṣā̍ te su̱taḥ soma̱ḥ pari̍ṣiktā̱ madhū̍ni | yu̱ktvā vṛṣa̍bhyāṁ vṛṣabha kṣitī̱nāṁ hari̍bhyāṁ yāhi pra̱vatopa̍ ma̱drik ||
english: Mount the bull-chariot, O bull; your soma is pressed, the honey-draughts are poured out. Harnessing your two bull-like bays, O bull of the peoples, come down the slope towards us!

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ ya̱jño de̍va̱yā a̱yam mi̱yedha̍ i̱mā brahmā̍ṇy a̱yam i̍ndra̱ soma̍ḥ | stī̱rṇam ba̱rhir ā tu śa̍kra̱ pra yā̍hi̱ pibā̍ ni̱ṣadya̱ vi mu̍cā̱ harī̍ i̱ha ||
english: This sacrifice is for the god, this is the oblation; these are the prayers, this is the soma, O Indra. The kusa grass is strewn — come forward, O mighty one; sit and drink; unyoke your bays here.

sanskrit: o suṣṭu̍ta indra yāhy a̱rvāṅ upa̱ brahmā̍ṇi mā̱nyasya̍ kā̱roḥ | vi̱dyāma̱ vasto̱r ava̍sā gṛ̱ṇanto̍ vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: Come hither, O well-praised Indra, to the prayers of Mānyasya the poet. May we know the help at dawn as we praise — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: yad dha̱ syā ta̍ indra śru̱ṣṭir asti̱ yayā̍ ba̱bhūtha̍ jari̱tṛbhya̍ ū̱tī | mā na̱ḥ kāma̍m ma̱haya̍nta̱m ā dha̱g viśvā̍ te aśyā̱m pary āpa̍ ā̱yoḥ ||
english: If, O Indra, you indeed have that readiness to hear by which you have been the helper of praisers — do not burn up our desire when it is growing great; may we attain all the things you have, with the life-span.

sanskrit: na ghā̱ rājendra̱ ā da̍bhan no̱ yā nu svasā̍rā kṛ̱ṇava̍nta̱ yonau̍ | āpa̍ś cid asmai su̱tukā̍ aveṣa̱n gama̍n na̱ indra̍ḥ sa̱khyā vaya̍ś ca ||
english: Truly no king, O Indra, has deceived us — those who are now making sisters in the womb. Even the waters, easily flowing, have gone for him; Indra has come with friendship and with birds.

sanskrit: jetā̱ nṛbhi̱r indra̍ḥ pṛ̱tsu śūra̱ḥ śrotā̱ hava̱ṁ nādha̍mānasya kā̱roḥ | prabha̍rtā̱ ratha̍ṁ dā̱śuṣa̍ upā̱ka udya̍ntā̱ giro̱ yadi̍ ca̱ tmanā̱ bhūt ||
english: Indra, the hero, conquers in battles with men; he hears the call of the poet who implores. He brings the chariot near to the worshipper — if the raised songs should come of themselves.

sanskrit: e̱vā nṛbhi̱r indra̍ḥ suśrava̱syā pra̍khā̱daḥ pṛ̱kṣo a̱bhi mi̱triṇo̍ bhūt | sa̱ma̱rya i̱ṣaḥ sta̍vate̱ vivā̍ci satrāka̱ro yaja̍mānasya̱ śaṁsa̍ḥ ||
english: Thus Indra with men, through desire for good fame, becomes a bold helper against those who are hostile. In the encounter of courses he is praised with voice; the all-achieving glory of the sacrificer is proclaimed.

sanskrit: tvayā̍ va̱yam ma̍ghavann indra̱ śatrū̍n a̱bhi ṣyā̍ma maha̱to manya̍mānān | tvaṁ trā̱tā tvam u̍ no vṛ̱dhe bhū̍r vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: Through you, O Maghavan Indra, may we overpower the enemies who think themselves great. Be you our protector; be you also for our increase — may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.

sanskrit: pū̱rvīr a̱haṁ śa̱rada̍ḥ śaśramā̱ṇā do̱ṣā vasto̍r u̱ṣaso̍ ja̱raya̍ntīḥ | mi̱nāti̱ śriya̍ṁ jari̱mā ta̱nūnā̱m apy ū̱ nu patnī̱r vṛṣa̍ṇo jagamyuḥ ||
english: I have grown weary through many autumns, through nights and days that make the dawns old. Old age diminishes the beauty of bodies — even so now the wives should have gone to their bull-husbands.

sanskrit: ye ci̱d dhi pūrva̍ ṛta̱sāpa̱ āsa̍n sā̱kaṁ de̱vebhi̱r ava̍dann ṛ̱tāni̍ | te ci̱d avā̍sur na̱hy anta̍m ā̱puḥ sam ū̱ nu patnī̱r vṛṣa̍bhir jagamyuḥ ||
english: Even those former ones who were watchers of ṛta, who declared the sacred truths together with the gods — even those came down, for they never reached the end. Now too the wives have come together with their bull-husbands.

sanskrit: na mṛṣā̍ śrā̱ntaṁ yad ava̍nti de̱vā viśvā̱ it spṛdho̍ a̱bhy a̍śnavāva | jayā̱ved atra̍ śa̱tanī̍tham ā̱jiṁ yat sa̱myañcā̍ mithu̱nāv a̱bhy ajā̍va ||
english: Not in vain does the weary one whom the gods help — we two shall win all contests. Here let us win the hundred-guided race as the pair of us, united as a couple, have rushed forward together.

sanskrit: na̱dasya̍ mā rudha̱taḥ kāma̱ āga̍nn i̱ta ājā̍to a̱muta̱ḥ kuta̍ś cit | lopā̍mudrā̱ vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ nī ri̍ṇāti̱ dhīra̱m adhī̍rā dhayati śva̱santa̍m ||
english: The desire of the roaring, pressing one has come to me — born here, from here, or from wherever. Lopāmudrā draws the bull downward; the rash one sucks the wise man as he sleeps.

sanskrit: i̱maṁ nu soma̱m anti̍to hṛ̱tsu pī̱tam upa̍ bruve | yat sī̱m āga̍ś cakṛ̱mā tat su mṛ̍ḻatu pulu̱kāmo̱ hi martya̍ḥ ||
english: This soma now drunk close by and deep in the heart I invoke. Whatever transgression we have committed, may that be forgiven by him — for mortal man has many desires.

sanskrit: a̱gastya̱ḥ khana̍mānaḥ kha̱nitrai̍ḥ pra̱jām apa̍tya̱m bala̍m i̱cchamā̍naḥ | u̱bhau varṇā̱v ṛṣi̍r u̱graḥ pu̍poṣa sa̱tyā de̱veṣv ā̱śiṣo̍ jagāma ||
english: Agastya, digging with his tools, desiring offspring, progeny and strength — the mighty seer has nourished both castes, and has gone to the gods with true prayers fulfilled.

sanskrit: yu̱vo rajā̍ṁsi su̱yamā̍so̱ aśvā̱ ratho̱ yad vā̱m pary arṇā̍ṁsi̱ dīya̍t | hi̱ra̱ṇyayā̍ vām pa̱vaya̍ḥ pruṣāya̱n madhva̱ḥ piba̍ntā u̱ṣasa̍ḥ sacethe ||
english: Your realms, your well-yoked horses, your chariot — when it flies around the seas for you two — with golden rims sprinkling you, drinking the honey, you two follow the dawns.

sanskrit: yu̱vam atya̱syāva̍ nakṣatho̱ yad vipa̍tmano̱ narya̍sya̱ praya̍jyoḥ | svasā̱ yad vā̍ṁ viśvagūrtī̱ bharā̍ti̱ vājā̱yeṭṭe̍ madhupāv i̱ṣe ca̍ ||
english: You two go beyond the stallion when you go to the manly one whose wings spread wide, worthy of reverence. When the sister who is praised by all brings you two, O honey-drinkers, for the prize and the refreshment.

sanskrit: yu̱vam paya̍ u̱sriyā̍yām adhattam pa̱kvam ā̱māyā̱m ava̱ pūrvya̱ṁ goḥ | a̱ntar yad va̱nino̍ vām ṛtapsū hvā̱ro na śuci̱r yaja̍te ha̱viṣmā̍n ||
english: You two placed the milk in the cow Uśriyā, the ripe within the raw, the ancient one. When among the trees the truthful-dripping one calls upon you two — as a clear, unwinding one — the oblation-bearer worships.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ha̍ gha̱rmam madhu̍manta̱m atra̍ye̱ 'po na kṣodo̍ 'vṛṇītam e̱ṣe | tad vā̍ṁ narāv aśvinā̱ paśva̍ïṣṭī̱ rathye̍va ca̱krā prati̍ yanti̱ madhva̍ḥ ||
english: You two have indeed chosen the honey-sweet warm drink for Atri, like waters for the flood to approach. That, O Aśvins, O heroes, seeking cattle — like chariot wheels your praises return with honey.

sanskrit: ā vā̍ṁ dā̱nāya̍ vavṛtīya dasrā̱ gor ohe̍ṇa tau̱gryo na jivri̍ḥ ||  a̱paḥ kṣo̱ṇī sa̍cate̱ māhi̍nā vāṁ jū̱rṇo vā̱m akṣu̱r aṁha̍so yajatrā ||
english: I would turn toward you two for your gift, O wondrous Aśvins, like a worn old man aided by Tugra's son. The great earth follows the waters of you two; worn out, your eye, O worshipful ones, has suffered from distress.

sanskrit: ni yad yu̱vethe̍ ni̱yuta̍ḥ sudānū̱ upa̍ sva̱dhābhi̍ḥ sṛjatha̱ḥ pura̍ṁdhim | preṣa̱d veṣa̱d vāto̱ na sū̱rir ā ma̱he da̍de suvra̱to na vāja̍m ||
english: When you two set down your teams and let loose the mighty lady of intelligence with your own powers, O generous givers — then the sun-lord comes forward and backward like the wind; the good-vowed one obtains a great prize.

sanskrit: va̱yaṁ ci̱d dhi vā̍ṁ jari̱tāra̍ḥ sa̱tyā vi̍pa̱nyāma̍he̱ vi pa̱ṇir hi̱tāvā̍n | adhā̍ ci̱d dhi ṣmā̍śvināv anindyā pā̱tho hi ṣmā̍ vṛṣaṇā̱v anti̍devam ||
english: We too, being truly your praisers, proclaim you to be true; the chanter is well-placed. And indeed, O blameless Aśvins, you two drink; for you two bulls drink right up to the god.

sanskrit: yu̱vāṁ ci̱d dhi ṣmā̍śvinā̱v anu̱ dyūn viru̍drasya pra̱srava̍ṇasya sā̱tau | a̱gastyo̍ na̱rāṁ nṛṣu̱ praśa̍sta̱ḥ kārā̍dhunīva citayat sa̱hasrai̍ḥ ||
english: Indeed you two Aśvins for days in the winning of the stream of Virudra — Agastya, praised among men as a hero among heroes, has illuminated you like a Kārādhunī with thousands.

sanskrit: pra yad vahe̍the mahi̱nā ratha̍sya̱ pra sya̍ndrā yātho̱ manu̍ṣo̱ na hotā̍ | dha̱ttaṁ sū̱ribhya̍ u̱ta vā̱ svaśvya̱ṁ nāsa̍tyā rayi̱ṣāca̍ḥ syāma ||
english: When you two carry forward with the greatness of the chariot, when you two race like the Hotā of Manu — grant good horses to the sun-lords and wealth; may we be winners of riches, O Nāsatyas.

sanskrit: taṁ vā̱ṁ ratha̍ṁ va̱yam a̱dyā hu̍vema̱ stomai̍r aśvinā suvi̱tāya̱ navya̍m | ari̍ṣṭanemi̱m pari̱ dyām i̍yā̱naṁ vi̱dyāme̱ṣaṁ vṛ̱jana̍ṁ jī̱radā̍num ||
english: That chariot of yours, O Aśvins, we would invoke today anew with praises for our welfare — it whose rim is unhurt, going around heaven: may we know the refreshment, the broad space giving long life.
